what: Voice cloning on CPU through bolo (core.synthesize with a saved voice), server/tools/measure_cloning.py
machine: 4 vCPU x86_64 (Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz), no GPU, 15 GB RAM, shared with other jobs (a browser benchmark and test suites ran at the same time, so speeds are pessimistic)
runtime: llama.cpp b12375 llama-server (upstream release, CPU build), started by bolo
references: LibriSpeech dev-clean (CC BY 4.0) speakers 2277 and 84, three utterances each (about 15 s), with their transcripts, cleaned as POST /api/v1/voices does

fields.similarity: speaker similarity of the output to the reference (pyannote-3.0-eres2net; same real person scores 0.45-0.93, median 0.80; 0.50+ = same speaker)
fields.impostor: highest similarity of the output to any of the 14 other LibriSpeech speakers (5 clips each)
fields.stock_similarity: the model's first catalog voice (no cloning of this reference) against the reference
fields.rtf: wall time / audio, one run after a warm-up
fields.ttfa_ms: time to the first audio chunk
fields.wer: round trip: moonshine-tiny-en (English) or whisper-base (other languages) against the text

watermark_check.what: Is Resemble's Perth watermark in Chatterbox output through bolo?
watermark_check.tool: resemble-perth 1.0.1 (PerthImplicitWatermarker, CPU PyTorch), get_watermark on the WAV bolo wrote (bolo speak, voice libri-84); positive control: the same clip after apply_watermark
watermark_check.conclusion: llama.cpp's Chatterbox does not watermark; the catalog no longer says it does.
